title: A finite inverse tetrahedron detects equivalences
statement:
Use quasicategories, equivalence edges, and standard simplices from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Form the simplicial set
$$Q=\Delta^0\amalg_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}}\Delta^3\amalg_{\Delta^{\{1,3\}}}\Delta^0,$$
collapsing each displayed opposite edge to a vertex, and write $c:\Delta^1\to Q$ for the image of the central edge $\{1,2\}$. For every small quasicategory $D$ and every equivalence edge $e:\Delta^1\to D$, there is a simplicial map $f:Q\to D$ with $fc=e$. Every simplicial map $Q\to D$ carries every edge of $Q$ to an equivalence in $D$.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Proposition B.1.6, forward direction (3) and reverse direction (A1), printed pp.1473-1474. The first assertion is the extension of the central edge into the Kan core; the second is the inverse diagram chase. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Let $e:a\to b$ be the prescribed equivalence. By the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], choose an inverse $u:b\to a$ and two $2$-simplices with ordered boundary triples $(u,e,1_b)$ and $(e,u,1_a)$, where a triple lists edges $01,12,02$. Give vertices $0,1,2,3$ the values $b,a,b,a$. On face $012$ use the first inverse triangle, on face $123$ the second, and on face $013$ the degenerate triangle $(u,1_a,u)$ obtained by repeating the target of $u$. These faces agree on their pairwise intersections: the common edges $12,13,01$ are respectively $e,1_a,u$. Consequently they define a map $\Lambda_1^3\to D$ (faces opposite vertices $0,2,3$). This is direct gluing on the union of the three faces; compatibility on their edge intersections also gives compatibility on every smaller simplex.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Proposition B.1.6, (3) and (A1), printed pp.1473-1474; explicit agent expansion of the inverse tetrahedron and diagram chase.

proof.text: The horn in step 1 is inner, since $0<1<3$. The defining horn-filling property of the quasicategory [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives $\sigma:\Delta^3\to D$ extending it. Its edges $02$ and $13$ are exactly the degenerate edges at $b$ and $a$, while its edge $12$ is exactly $e$. Thus $\sigma$ is constant on each of $\Delta^{\{0,2\}}$ and $\Delta^{\{1,3\}}$. It descends to $f:Q\to D$: in degree $m$ send the class of a simplex of $\Delta^3$ to its image under $\sigma$, and send the simplex of each attached $\Delta^0$ to the corresponding constant simplex. The assignments agree on the two collapsed edges in every degree and commute with face and degeneracy operators, so they give a simplicial map with $fc=e$.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Proposition B.1.6, (3) and (A1), printed pp.1473-1474; explicit agent expansion of the inverse tetrahedron and diagram chase.

proof.text: Now let $F:Q\to D$ be any simplicial map and restrict it to $\Delta^3$. Put $x=F(0)=F(2)$ and $y=F(1)=F(3)$, and denote its edges $01,12,23,03$ by $u:x\to y$, $v:y\to x$, $w:x\to y$, $z:x\to y$. The edges $02,13$ are the degenerate identities at $x,y$. In the edge-and-triangle category $hD$ of [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus], the four faces $012,123,013,023$ therefore give, respectively, $$[v]\circ[u]=1_x,\qquad [w]\circ[v]=1_y,\qquad [z]=[u],\qquad [z]=[w].$$ These equalities use precisely the triangle relations and the relations identifying degenerate edges with identities in that cited statement.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Proposition B.1.6, (3) and (A1), printed pp.1473-1474; explicit agent expansion of the inverse tetrahedron and diagram chase.

proof.text: The last two equalities imply $[u]=[z]=[w]$. Substituting into the first two shows that for each $r\in\{u,w,z\}$, $$[v]\circ[r]=1_x,\qquad [r]\circ[v]=1_y.$$ In particular $[u]$ and $[v]$ are mutual inverses. This is substitution of the displayed relations in the ordinary category $hD$ defined in [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus]; it does not assert equality of the actual edges $u,w,z$.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Proposition B.1.6, (3) and (A1), printed pp.1473-1474; explicit agent expansion of the inverse tetrahedron and diagram chase.

proof.text: Apply the exact triangle criterion of [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus] to both equations in step 4. For each $r\in\{u,w,z\}$ it gives $2$-simplices with boundary triples $(r,v,1_x)$ and $(v,r,1_y)$. Thus $r$ is an equivalence edge by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; taking $r=u$ also proves that $v$ is an equivalence, with inverse $u$. The remaining edges $02,13$, and the images of vertex degeneracies, are identities, whose inverse triangles are the constant $2$-simplices. There are no other edges to check: the pushout defining $Q$ is the degreewise quotient described in step 2, so every $1$-simplex is represented either by an edge or a vertex degeneracy of $\Delta^3$, or by the unique (degenerate) edge of an attached $\Delta^0$. Hence $F$ sends every edge of $Q$ to an equivalence.

source.place: Higher Algebra, proof of Proposition B.1.6, (3) and (A1), printed pp.1473-1474; explicit agent expansion of the inverse tetrahedron and diagram chase.

lean.statement: theorem finite_inverse_tetrahedron (D : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory D] : (∀ e : (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}) ⟶ D, IsEquivalenceEdge D (yonedaEquiv e) → ∃ f : inverseTetrahedron.{u} ⟶ D, inverseTetrahedronCentralEdge ≫ f = e) ∧ (∀ (f : inverseTetrahedron.{u} ⟶ D) (a : inverseTetrahedron.{u} _⦋1⦌), IsEquivalenceEdge D (f.app _ a))
